channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: F5 Issues Advisory for Multiple BIG-IP Vulnerabilities
item.description: F5 released advisory AV26-1178 exposing multiple vulnerabilities in BIG-IP, APM, SSL Orchestrator, PEM, CNF, and Next for Kubernetes versions up to 21.1.0. The flaws allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via malformed configuration data, with CVSS scores up to 9.8, and are documented.

item.title: PHP Releases Patch for 7 Critical RCE Flaws
item.description: PHP Foundation released a patch for seven critical flaws that could allow remote code execution on affected deployments. The most severe flaw, CVE-2026-115560, scores CVSS 9.2 and stems from improper input validation that permits arbitrary code execution and file modification. All supported PHP versions have the update available; administrators should apply the patch immediately to mitigate exploitation.

item.title: European Commission confirms cyberattack, says hackers used AI tool
item.description: POLITICO had reported CERT-EU had identified the attackers’ use of ARTEX, an open-source AI hacking platform that the FBI last week warned was being used both by criminals and state-sponsored groups.

item.title: VMware vCenter Auth Bypass Vulnerability Fixed
item.description: A critical flaw in VMware vCenter, scoring CVSS 9.8, allows network attackers to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the management console. The vulnerability exploits a flaw in the authentication mechanism, enabling attackers to control ESX hosts and virtual machines without credentials. All supported vCenter branches have patched releases; administrators should update immediately and verify authentication logs for anomalies.

item.title: Ransomware Warning Signs Before Encryption
item.description: Acronis identifies five early warning signs of ransomware activity that occur before encryption or data theft. These indicators include credential theft, lateral movement, and attempts to disable security controls, allowing attackers to establish persistence. Security teams should monitor for these behaviors, enforce least-privilege access, and implement continuous monitoring to detect and contain intrusions early.

item.title: NGINX2Root Vulnerabilities Enable Remote Code Execution
item.description: Two critical NGINX vulnerabilities, collectively known as nginx2root, allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code remotely on vulnerable web servers. Researchers chained the flaws with a Linux kernel bug to elevate privileges to root, demonstrating a full system compromise. All supported NGINX releases have patches; administrators should apply the update and monitor for kernel exploitation attempts.

item.title: PHP Warns of Critical Security Flaws Affecting All Supported Versions, Urges Users to Update
item.description: The PHP security team has warned of vulnerabilities across all branches covered by its November 19, 2026 security update, with the most severe issues rated critical. The team urged website operators and hosting providers to update promptly. The critical flaws require non-default settings or uncommon setups, so not every installation faces the same risk.

item.title: Drupal Fixes Installer Flaw Enabling Site Takeover
item.description: Drupal core contains a critical installer flaw that permits unauthenticated attackers to trigger a site reinstallation and take over the site. The vulnerability requires specific configuration conditions and can lead to remote code execution if the installer is invoked without proper safeguards. All supported Drupal branches have patched releases; site administrators should apply the update and verify installer access controls.

item.title: Nvidia Denies Gentlemen Ransomware Claim
item.description: Gentlemen ransomware group listed Nvidia as a victim, alleging a compromise of its systems. No evidence of exploitation or data exfiltration was found, and the claim lacks supporting proof of a vulnerability or breach. Nvidia confirmed no compromise and urged stakeholders to monitor for potential phishing or credential theft attempts.

item.title: BADBOX 3.0 Malware Infects Android TV Boxes to Generate 40 Billion Fraudulent Ad Requests Daily
item.description: Low-cost Android streaming boxes helped power an advertising fraud operation that generated roughly 40 billion bid requests a day at its peak. Known as BADBOX 3.0, the campaign used infected devices to play video ads outside the visible screen while making the traffic look as though it came from legitimate streaming apps.

item.title: ARMORY CASTLE Exploits vSphere
item.description: Written by: Jayson Frost, Bryce Greathouse, Dhanesh Kizhakkinan, John Palmisano, Steve Rasch, Daniel Sislo, John Wolfram Introduction On Oct. 15, 2026, Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) published a blog post detailing recent activity in which the suspected PRC-nexus threat actor ARMORY CASTLE (formerly tracked as UNC5221) exploited CVE-2026-102764, a zero-day vulnerability in BeyondTrust Remote Support, which was patched in BT26-05 .

item.title: Russian Operation Steals Bank, IRS Credentials from PCs
item.description: A Russian-speaking cybercrime group has stolen login credentials for US banks, the IRS, and Social Security from infected Windows PCs. Victims were ordinary users; many employed password managers and MFA, yet attackers still captured credentials through malware, without breaching any institution. Defenders should harden endpoint security, enforce multi-factor authentication, and monitor for credential-stealing malware to prevent similar thefts.

item.title: Ubuntu 24.04 Kernel Update Addresses Critical IPv4, Bridge, Netfilter Vulnerabilities
item.description: Ubuntu 24.04 users must install the latest kernel update to patch critical vulnerabilities affecting IPv4 networking, Ethernet bridge, Netfilter, and XFRM subsystems. The flaws, CVE-2026-98432 and CVE-2026-99999, could enable privilege escalation or denial of service if exploited by attackers. Immediate kernel upgrade is recommended to mitigate potential compromise and maintain system security.

item.title: Ubuntu Patches Kernel Vulnerabilities in IPv4, Bridge, Netfilter, SCTP
item.description: Ubuntu 24.04 USN-9170-1 fixes Linux kernel flaws affecting IPv4 networking, Ethernet bridge, Netfilter, SCTP, and XFRM subsystems. The vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-64564, CVE-2026-98432, and CVE-2026-99999, could enable privilege escalation or denial of service if exploited by an attacker. Apply the kernel update immediately to patch the affected subsystems and prevent potential compromise.

item.title: Ukraine Arrests Ransomware Network Extorting $40M
item.description: Ukrainian authorities arrested four suspects linked to an international ransomware network that extorted over $40 million from U.S. oil and healthcare firms. The group used credential theft and encrypted data to demand ransom, targeting critical infrastructure and causing significant financial loss. Law enforcement seized ransom payments and seized infrastructure, and the operators face prosecution under Ukrainian cybercrime statutes.

item.title: Gatekeeper Asymmetry Makes LLMs More Vulnerable
item.description: The paper introduces gatekeeper asymmetry doom, asserting that when input vetting is weaker than processing, vulnerability is inevitable. Authors illustrate the principle with examples across security domains, showing limited input validation can cause catastrophic failures in powerful LLMs. The study urges stronger gatekeeping and hard-problem reliance to mitigate asymmetry in advanced AI systems.

item.title: Cisco Expressway Devices Hacked After PoC Release
item.description: Attackers compromised clustered Cisco Expressway devices at a Russian organization shortly after a public proof-of-concept was released. The flaw allowed authenticated remote code execution via malformed SIP messages, enabling attackers to gain privileged access and prepare lateral movement tools. Cisco issued a patch in the following security advisory, and security teams should update firmware and disable unused SIP services.

item.title: Drupal Fixes Critical Remote Code Execution Flaw
item.description: Drupal Security Team patched a critical remote code execution flaw that could let attackers seize control of vulnerable sites. The vulnerability, a buffer overflow in a core module, carries a CVSS score of 9.8 and has a publicly available proof-of-concept exploit. Administrators must apply the latest Drupal update immediately and confirm the core module is patched to prevent remote takeover.

item.title: CISA Warns Hackers Are Actively Exploiting Four Flaws in Synology, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and REDCap
item.description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added four flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on November 18, 2026, after finding evidence that attackers were already exploiting them. The entries cover Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM), BerriAI LiteLLM, Apache Axis and Vanderbilt University’s Research Electronic Data Capture platform, better known as REDCap.

item.title: Chrome 158 Fixes Six Critical Flaws
item.description: Google released Chrome 158, addressing 204 security issues, including six critical vulnerabilities. Two of the critical flaws were identified using AI-assisted analysis, highlighting the role of machine learning in vulnerability discovery. Users should update to Chrome 158 immediately to mitigate the disclosed vulnerabilities and maintain secure browsing and protect against exploitation.

item.title: Microsoft 365 MFA Bypassed via Device Code Phishing
item.description: Hackers hijacked Microsoft 365 accounts by sending fake payment notices that redirect users to a legitimate Microsoft sign-in page. The attack exploits the device code flow’s lack of MFA enforcement, letting attackers obtain tokens without credential verification. Microsoft recommends disabling device code authentication for sensitive workloads and enforcing MFA; users should verify invoice authenticity before signing in.

item.title: StepSecurity Raises $20M for Supply Chain Defense
item.description: StepSecurity announced a $20M funding round to expand its supply chain protection platform. The capital will accelerate development and distribution of its security solutions, targeting supply chain risk mitigation for enterprises and supporting rapid scaling. No immediate patch or vulnerability; the announcement signals investment in future defensive capabilities within the cybersecurity market.

item.title: Apache Roller, Axis Flaws Exploited in Confluence Attacks
item.description: Attackers have exploited critical vulnerabilities in Apache Roller and Axis, targeting Confluence Data Center deployments. The Axis flaw permits remote code execution through malformed XML, while the Roller issue allows unauthorized file uploads, both with CVSS scores above 8.0. Administrators should apply vendor patches, disable XML processing if possible, and enforce strict file-type validation to mitigate exploitation.

item.title: Palo Alto PAN-OS Exposed to PHP RCE Vulnerabilities
item.description: Palo Alto Networks confirmed attackers exploited two PHP flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, on PAN-OS interfaces exposed to the internet. Both flaws allow unauthenticated remote code execution on the web server, enabling attackers to run arbitrary code without credentials. Palo Alto released patches; administrators should apply updates immediately and restrict internet exposure of management interfaces.

item.title: Microsoft Tests Edge Lockdown Mode Disabling GPU APIs
item.description: Microsoft is testing an Edge Lockdown Mode that disables WebGL, WebGL2, and WebGPU APIs to shrink the browser attack surface. The feature removes GPU-accelerated rendering paths that could be leveraged for memory corruption or side-channel attacks, preserving core functionality. Microsoft plans to roll out the mode in a future update; security teams should monitor release notes for configuration options.

item.title: BackBox Linux 10 brings new hacking tools and Ubuntu 26.04 support
item.description: BackBox Linux is a free, open source penetration testing distribution made by BackBox, a non-profit community project that keeps its own repositories of ethical hacking tools. On November 19 the project released version 10, codenamed Resolute Raccoon. It’s built for compatibility with Ubuntu 26.04 LTS and ships with the Linux 7.0 kernel and the Xfce 4.20 desktop.

item.title: N-Able Breach: Management Access Disabled
item.description: N-Able confirmed unauthorized access to a single server in its Mail Assure and SpamExperts hosted cloud, targeting interfaces across the Americas, Europe, and Asia-Pacific. Email filtering remained operational, allowing customers to send and receive mail, while administrators lost access and N-Able disabled portals pending investigation.

item.title: Splunk Releases Patches for 140 Vulnerabilities
item.description: Splunk released security updates addressing nearly 140 critical and high-severity flaws across its three core products. The vulnerabilities enabled authentication bypass, remote code execution, and privilege escalation, with CVSS scores ranging from 7.0 to 9.8, and public proof-of-concept exploits were available for several. All affected products now ship patched versions; administrators should apply the updates immediately to mitigate the risks.

item.title: Microsoft Issues Workaround for Office Launch Issues Post-Hotpatch
item.description: Microsoft confirmed a Windows 11 hotpatch caused installation and launch failures in Office and other third-party apps. The problem originates from a corrupted registry update that interferes with startup, but does not expose data or allow code execution.

item.title: F5 Patches Five NGINX2Root Flaws
item.description: F5 Networks released emergency patches for five NGINX2Root vulnerabilities that enable remote, unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected systems. Public proof-of-concept exploits have surfaced, confirming the flaws’ exploitability and prompting immediate remediation by affected customers. F5 recommends applying the latest firmware updates and verifying patch deployment to mitigate the risk of code execution.

item.title: GTA 6 scams are after your Google password, money, and crypto wallet
item.description: Scammers are using the GTA 6 launch to steal Google passwords, sell game keys that may never arrive, and get players to connect crypto wallets. Stefan Dasic, a senior malware research engineer at Malwarebytes, tracked the lures.

item.title: Ukraine arrests key members of ransomware gang that extorted $40.5 million posing as IT support
item.description: Four key members of a ransomware group that took more than $40.5 million from at least 28 companies have been detained in Ukraine. The arrests followed an investigation that Ukrainian police ran with the FBI for more than two years.

item.title: Ubuntu Releases Kernel Patch for Multiple Azure Vulnerabilities
item.description: Ubuntu issued a kernel update addressing several vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to compromise Azure-hosted systems. The flaws span USB gadget drivers, memory management, various architectures, and file system components, with no confirmed exploitation in the wild. All affected subsystems are fixed in the latest kernel release; administrators should apply the update promptly to mitigate potential compromise.

item.title: Hackers Target European Commission with ARTEX AI Tool in Major Cyberattack
item.description: A cyberattack on the European Commission disrupted staff services for more than 10 days, leaving some employees unable to submit timesheets, request leave, or enter salary information. The EU’s cybersecurity service, CERT-EU, found that hackers used an AI tool called ARTEX, POLITICO reported on November 19, 2026.

item.title: Scattered Spider Uses Phishing, SIM-Swap Tactics
item.description: Scattered Spider employed fake text messages and SIM-swap operations to compromise user accounts and intercept authentication codes. The actor leveraged social engineering to bypass two-factor authentication, enabling unauthorized access to corporate systems; no public exploit or CVE was disclosed. Security teams should verify phone number ownership, enable device-based authentication, and monitor for SIM-swap activity to mitigate similar attacks.

item.title: Hackers Breach N-able Cloud Server, Disrupting Email Security Management Across 3 Regions
item.description: N-able on Wednesday disclosed that unknown threat actors gained unauthorized access to one of the servers in the Mail Assure and Spam Experts Hosted Cloud, causing it to disable management interfaces and APIs. "We have taken steps to mitigate the threat and are continuing to harden our services to reduce the risk of recurrence," N-able said.

item.title: NVIDIA Investigates Gentlemen Leak Claims
item.description: NVIDIA is investigating claims that the Gentlemen ransomware group listed the company on its dark-web data-leak site, implying a possible breach. The leak site reportedly contains sensitive data, but NVIDIA has not confirmed any compromise or the breach’s scope. NVIDIA advises customers to monitor for suspicious activity and apply forthcoming security updates while the investigation continues.

item.title: Hackers Deploy Overlord RAT That Survives Windows Resets and Crashes Systems When Terminated
item.description: A financially motivated hacking group is deploying Overlord RAT, a Windows remote access trojan that can return after a victim uses “Reset this PC.” The malware can also trigger a blue screen if a user or security tool forcibly ends its process.

item.title: Ruby Fixes 7 Regex/String Flaws, Warns 5 RCE PoCs
item.description: Ruby released patches for seven memory-safety flaws in its regular expression engine and string case-conversion code. Five of those defects have proof-of-concept exploits that allow crafted input to trigger remote code execution on affected systems. The maintainers advise users to upgrade to the fixed Ruby versions immediately to eliminate the RCE risk.

item.title: ruby2ßhell: Critical One-Byte Heap Overflow in Ruby Could Allow RCE Attacks
item.description: Ruby has patched a critical memory corruption flaw that can allow remote code execution (RCE) on vulnerable servers. Tracked as GHSA-34m4-m9fh-gqp5 and named ruby2ßhell by Veria Labs, the flaw affects Ruby’s string case conversion code.

item.title: Splunk Fixes Critical RCE and Auth Bypass in SOAR
item.description: Splunk released patches for its SOAR and Enterprise platforms to address a critical remote code execution flaw and a separate authentication bypass. The SOAR vulnerability, CVE-2026-131253, scored 9.9/10 and requires privileged accounts, while the Enterprise flaw, CVE-2026-76535, allows unauthenticated users to execute searches. Administrators should apply the latest updates immediately to eliminate the high-risk code execution and privilege escalation vectors.

item.title: Ruby Releases Patch for Seven RCE Vulnerabilities
item.description: Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13, and 3.3.14 were updated to fix seven vulnerabilities in the language’s regex engine and string case-conversion code. The flaws enable remote code execution by allowing attackers to run arbitrary code within vulnerable Ruby processes, with proof-of-concept demonstrations already available. Users should upgrade to the patched releases immediately to prevent exploitation of the critical RCE vectors.

item.title: US enlists private firms to cut scammers off from victims’ cash
item.description: Stopping victims’ money before it reaches foreign scam, cybercrime and sextortion networks is the goal of a new US unit launched by the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF). The Threat Disruption Center is part of the HSTF’s National Coordination Center (NCC) in Fairfax, Virginia.

item.title: Researcher Demonstrates RCE in PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle
item.description: A researcher demonstrated remote code execution exploits against PostgreSQL, MySQL, and Oracle databases using low-privilege accounts. The attacks leveraged memory-corruption bugs in the database engines, allowing code execution on the server without table read permissions. No vendor patches are currently available; administrators should restrict low-privilege access and monitor for anomalous activity until mitigations are released.

item.title: CISA Adds Four Exploited Vulnerabilities
item.description: CISA added four actively exploited vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, affecting Synology DSM, BerriAI LiteLLM, Apache Axis, and Vanderbilt REDCap systems. The flaws enable ransomware, cryptomining, and LLMjacking attacks, with evidence of active exploitation in the wild. CISA urges affected organizations to apply vendor patches, monitor for suspicious activity, and maintain up-to-date security configurations.

item.title: Africa Leads Global Cyber Attack Rankings
item.description: Threat intelligence indicates Africa now tops global attack rankings, with Nigeria’s incidents more than doubling from the previous year. The spike encompasses phishing, ransomware, and credential-stealing campaigns, placing Angola and Kenya among the top five most attacked nations. Defenders should enhance regional threat monitoring, strengthen endpoint defenses, and share indicators of compromise across national agencies.

item.title: PHP Issues Critical Update for CVE-2026-115560 RCE
item.description: PHP released a critical security update to address CVE-2026-115560, an RCE flaw affecting session upload progress. The vulnerability was publicly disclosed two days after the PHP2Shell patches, and proof-of-concept exploits are available. Administrators should apply the latest PHP patch immediately to eliminate the high-risk code execution vector in affected systems.

item.title: Chinese Hackers Upgrade EggStreme Malware With Silent Backdoor to Evade Security Detection
item.description: A suspected Chinese cyberespionage group has rebuilt its EggStreme malware framework, adding a Windows backdoor that waits for an incoming connection instead of calling out to an attacker-controlled server. Bitdefender’s November 18, 2026, report tracks the changes as the group continues to target government organizations in the Philippines.

item.title: ZDI-26-1038: (0Day) (Pwn2Own) United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP UpdateFirmware Out-Of-Bounds Write Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
item.description: This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability. The following CVEs are assigned: CVE-2026-131813.

item.title: Consumer Devices Breach OT Segmentation in Hospitals
item.description: Claroty found game consoles, Roku sticks, Teslas, and other consumer gadgets bypassing OT network segmentation in hospitals, factories, and commercial sites. Many devices are placed on production or guest segments, enabling attackers to move laterally to critical OT equipment without isolation. Teams should audit device placement, enforce strict segmentation, and monitor OT traffic to block lateral movement.
